title: Microsoft Purview: apply default SharePoint library labels to existing files (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, administrator-created policy, licensing and control operations are supported. Clarify that a label's visual markings are not applied to documents by service-side auto-labeling, and cite the separate Worldwide roadmap item.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Microsoft plans auto-labeling of existing SharePoint files using their document library's default sensitivity label.
claims.quote: Enables auto‑labeling of existing SharePoint files to match the default sensitivity label configured on their document library.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes closing labeling gaps for data at rest without relying on manual user labeling.
claims.quote: This helps organizations close labeling gaps for data at rest and ensure consistent, secure‑by‑default protection across SharePoint libraries—without relying on manual user labeling.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn documents an administrator-created auto-labeling policy that applies library defaults to eligible existing files.
claims.quote: To extend your default library label deployment to existing files, create an auto-labeling policy that applies the default sensitivity label from each selected SharePoint document library to eligible existing files at rest.

claims.claim: The existing-files policy is admin-opt-in: administrators create and turn on the policy before it labels files.
claims.quote: They're available across your organization from the moment you turn a policy on, which makes them suitable for labeling at scale.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk and cost
claims.claim: Microsoft instructs administrators to review this policy type's simulation results before turning it on.
claims.quote: Review the simulation results before you turn on the policy to confirm that the expected SharePoint sites, document libraries, default library labels, and files are included.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The existing-files capability uses service-side auto-labeling.
claims.quote: You want service-side labeling for files at rest, instead of relying on users to open or edit each file.

claims.claim: The separate library-default setting applies labels to new uploaded files.
claims.quote: Then, any new files uploaded to that library, or existing files edited in the library will have that label applied

claims.claim: The separate library-default setting applies labels to existing files when edited.
claims.quote: Then, any new files uploaded to that library, or existing files edited in the library will have that label applied

claims.claim: Unlabeled new or edited files can receive the library default.
claims.quote: if they don't already have a sensitivity label

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A library default can override a lower-priority automatically applied or policy-default label.
claims.quote: Automatically applied, lower priority | Yes; Default label from policy, lower priority | Yes

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The library-default page's override table says manually applied labels are not replaced.
claims.quote: Manually applied, any priority | No

claims.claim: The separate library-default page still lists existing files at rest as a limitation.
claims.quote: Doesn't apply to existing files at rest in SharePoint.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: impact
claims.claim: A label that applies encryption can change who can open a file.
claims.quote: Can be decrypted only by users authorized by the label's encryption settings.

claims.claim: An existing file could receive a label configured with markings or other settings.
claims.quote: If the labels you select are configured to use visual markings (headers, footers, watermarks), these markings aren't applied to documents when you use auto-labeling.
claims.fix: Replace 'Once such a policy runs, a label with encryption, markings or other settings could appear on many existing files.' with 'Once such a policy runs, many eligible existing files could receive the library default label and its encryption. Visual markings are not applied to documents by auto-labeling.'

claims.claim: The user-defined permissions configuration named on the library-default page is unsuitable for a library default.
claims.quote: Let users assign permissions when they apply the label and the checkbox In Word, PowerPoint, and Excel, prompt users to specify permissions is selected. This setting is sometimes referred to as "user-defined permissions".

claims.claim: A label with user access expiry other than Never does not support a library default.
claims.quote: some label configurations that apply encryption ... don't support a default sensitivity label for a SharePoint document library: ... User access to content expires is set to a value other than Never.

claims.claim: A label configured with Double Key Encryption does not support a library default.
claims.quote: some label configurations that apply encryption ... don't support a default sensitivity label for a SharePoint document library: ... Double Key Encryption is selected.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Site admin permissions are needed to apply and change a library's default sensitivity label.
claims.quote: Site admin permissions are needed to apply and change the sensitivity label in SharePoint.

claims.claim: Libraries with SharePoint Information Rights Management enabled cannot select a default sensitivity label.
claims.quote: If a library is enabled for IRM, you won't be able to select a default sensitivity label.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Applied sensitivity label file auditing event can identify library-default labeling.
claims.quote: use the audit log search tool and the Applied sensitivity label file auditing event from the Sensitivity label activities group.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: ActionScourceDetails 6 identifies the library-default application described on the library-default page.
claims.quote: identify the value for ActionScourceDetails. ... A value of 6 is used for when the label was applied because of the default sensitivity label for the document library.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document whether the existing-files policy uses the same ActionScourceDetails value.
claims.quote: Searched: "existing files" "library" "ActionScourceDetails"; read library-default monitoring and auto-labeling existing-files policy documentation. The value 6 is described for the separate library-default setting, not explicitly for this policy type.

claims.claim: The library-default label tooltip reads 'This file has been automatically labeled'.
claims.quote: the tooltip for the label name displays This file has been automatically labeled.

claims.claim: The same tooltip appears for labels applied by auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: It also displays when sensitivity labels are applied by using auto-labeling policies

claims.claim: The same tooltip appears for a user's default label from sensitivity label policies.
claims.quote: or as a result of a user's default label from sensitivity label policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not provide a specific government-cloud rollout window for this existing-files option.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview SharePoint existing files default library labels government cloud rollout GCC High DoD; read auto-labeling feature documentation and GCC, GCC High and DoD deployment search excerpts. No rollout window for this policy option was stated.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Sensitivity-label licensing is per-user and its requirements depend on the features used.
claims.quote: A number of different per-user subscriptions support sensitivity labels for Microsoft 365 apps and services, and the licensing requirements for users depend on the features you use.

claims.claim: Admins need a license to manage sensitivity labels, with feature-level requirements in the Purview service description.
claims.quote: Admins also need a license to manage sensitivity labels. ... see the Microsoft Purview service description ... for feature-level licensing requirements.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5 are among the qualifying licenses for client and service-side automatic sensitivity labeling.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5, Microsoft Purview Suite/GOV/FLW ... | Client and service-side automatic sensitivity labeling | Included

claims.claim: Office 365 E5/A5/G5 are among the qualifying licenses for client and service-side automatic sensitivity labeling.
claims.quote: Office 365 E5/A5/G5 ... | Client and service-side automatic sensitivity labeling | Included

claims.claim: The auto-labeling page says E3 and Business Premium do not include auto-labeling of files and emails and require an E5 / P2-tier add-on.
claims.quote: You have E3 or Business Premium. Auto-labeling of files and emails isn't included at this SKU. Sensitivity labels and manual labeling are — auto-labeling requires an E5 / P2-tier add-on.

claims.claim: A separate license or meter specific to the existing-files library-default option is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview SharePoint default library existing files labeling separate license price meter; read auto-labeling licensing, existing-files prerequisites, getting-started licensing and the Purview service description. Published requirements cover auto-labeling; no separate option-specific SKU or meter.

claims.claim: The library-default page's Requirements section names no license among its listed requirements.
claims.quote: Requirements: ... created and published ... sensitivity labels ... enabled sensitivity labels ... added support for PDFs ... IRM is not enabled ... Site admin permissions ... Files must contain content

claims.claim: Library defaults require created and published labels scoped to Files & other data assets.
claims.quote: You've created and published sensitivity labels that include the label scope of Files & other data assets and these labels are published to the users who will select a default sensitivity label for a SharePoint document library.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels must be enabled for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: You've enabled sensitivity labels for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.claim: PDF labeling requires adding PDF support in SharePoint.
claims.quote: To support sensitivity labels for PDFs, you've added support for PDFs in SharePoint.

claims.claim: Creating the existing-files policy requires permission to create and manage auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: You have permissions to create and manage auto-labeling policies.

claims.claim: The existing-files policy requires permission to read site and library metadata used to identify default labels.
claims.quote: You have permission to read the SharePoint site and document library metadata required to identify libraries with default sensitivity labels.

claims.claim: SharePoint document library > Settings > Library settings > Default sensitivity labels reaches the library-default control.
claims.quote: In SharePoint, navigate to the document library > Settings > Library settings. ... select Default sensitivity labels, and then select a label from the drop-down box.

claims.claim: POST https://<site-url>/_api/web/lists(guid'<library-guid>') with X-HTTP-Method: MERGE updates the library.
claims.quote: The following example shows how to update a list by using the MERGE method. ... POST https://{site_url}/_api/web/lists(guid'{list_guid}') ... X-HTTP-Method: "MERGE"

claims.claim: No tenant-level admin UI switch for document-library default labeling is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling admin center UI tenant existing files ActionScourceDetails default library; read library-default turn-off instructions and returned configuration excerpts. The tenant switch is documented through SharePoint PowerShell, not an admin UI.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling $true disables the existing library-default feature at tenant scope.
claims.quote: This is a tenant-level setting ... Set-SPOTenant ... DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling ... current SharePoint Online Management Shell: Set-SpoTenant -DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling $true

claims.claim: The tenant configuration change takes about 15 minutes to take effect.
claims.quote: As with all tenant-level configuration changes for SharePoint, it takes about 15 minutes for the change to take effect.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly confirmed that DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling stops the existing-files auto-labeling policy.
claims.quote: Searched: DisableDocumentLibraryDefaultLabeling admin center UI tenant existing files ActionScourceDetails default library; read library-default turn-off instructions and the existing-files policy section. The switch describes disabling defaults for new files, not stopping this policy type.

claims.claim: After disabling the library-default feature, an existing library's label selection remains but is deactivated.
claims.quote: The label selection for the document library remains but is deactivated so new files won't have the selected sensitivity label applied.

claims.claim: Disabling the library-default feature does not remove labels already applied as defaults.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels that were applied as a default label aren't removed.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Search reaches audit search.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. ... Select the Audit solution card. ... On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <date> -EndDate <date> -RecordType <ID> searches audit records by date range and record type.
claims.quote: runs Search-UnifiedAuditLog to search for audit log entries within a specified date range and record type. ... Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate 2023/03/12 -EndDate 2023/03/20 -RecordType <ID>

claims.claim: The audit row is read-only monitoring rather than a labeling configuration control.
claims.quote: you can use this cmdlet to search the audit log instead of using the search tool on the Audit page in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Updated list is the auditing event for changes to the library-default configuration.
claims.quote: To audit the configuration setting for this feature, use the Updated list auditing event from the SharePoint list activities group.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: The SharePoint Sensitivity column displays labels applied to files but its automatic-label tooltip is not unique to library defaults.
claims.quote: Use the SharePoint Sensitivity column to see the names of sensitivity labels applied to files. ... this tooltip isn't exclusive to the default sensitivity label for a document library.

claims.claim: The library-default setting is per-library and Extend protection on download, copy, or move is a different scenario that should not be selected here.
claims.quote: From the Library settings pane, select a sensitivity label and don't select the checkbox Extend protection on download, copy, or move. This setting is currently in preview and supports a different labeling scenario.

claims.claim: The REST update sets DefaultSensitivityLabelForLibrary to configure the library default.
claims.quote: For the default library label, set the DefaultSensitivityLabelForLibrary parameter by using REST API on a library.
